claims.source: First Air Force letter of 20 September 1957, reproduced in The UFO Evidence, 1964, in CIA-RDP81R00560R000100010001-0, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp81r00560r000100010001-0
claims.text: He held the post by September 1957 on a government correspondent's own address line. A letter on the letterhead 'Hq Sq Sec, First Air Force, Mitchel Air Force Base, NY', dated 20 September 1957, is addressed to 'Mr. Donald E. Keyhoe, Director NICAP, 1536 Connecticut Ave, N. W., Washington 6, D. C.' and transmits a quoted Air Force report of eight round objects sighted at Fort Devens, Massachusetts on 17 September 1957.

The volume states the Hillenkoetter connection as a personal one: 'Vice Admiral R. H. Hillenkoetter, USN (Ret.), a long-time acquaintance of Major Keyhoe, also served on the NICAP Board of Governors for five years.' It gives Keyhoe's own background as 'a graduate of the U. S. Naval Academy (class of 1920) and former Marine Corps aircraft and balloon pilot' and says his acquaintance with serving and retired officers is why several of its military cases could be detailed.

claims.source: CIA memorandum for record, 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects', CIA reading room document 0005516043, reading-room date 4 April 1958, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0005516043
claims.text: The CIA recorded a standing rule for handling him. A memorandum for record on 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects' notes that the Air Force was 'most insistent' on answering his letters itself, that 'the Air Force is endeavoring to impress upon Major Keyhoe and others in a similar position, that his office is the proper place to come for such information', and concludes: 'I think we can use this procedure as a precedent henceforth in all inquiries regarding UFO's.' The scan's OCR is imperfect and renders his surname inconsistently; the quoted sentences were legible.

claims.source: CIA reading room document 0000015416, 'Inquiry by Major Donald E. Keyhoe (deleted)', reading-room date 4 January 1959, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0000015416
claims.text: He put the question to the Director of Central Intelligence directly. An internal CIA memorandum of January 1959 quotes his memorandum of 13 March 1958 to the DCI asking whether CIA representatives had told UFO witnesses not to make their sightings public, and on what authority. The scan is partly illegible and no wording is quoted from it here.

label: Maj. Donald E. Keyhoe, USMC (Ret.)
narrative: Keyhoe ran the civilian organisation the board already carries as nicap, and he is the hinge between it and the former Director of Central Intelligence who sat on its board. A US Air Force headquarters letter of 20 September 1957 is addressed to him as Director NICAP at the organisation's Connecticut Avenue address, and NICAP's 1964 volume The UFO Evidence, in the copy the CIA filed, carries him on its masthead as director. He was a US Naval Academy graduate of 1920 and a former Marine Corps aircraft and balloon pilot, and the volume says plainly that his Navy connections are why several of its military cases are in it. In 1958 the CIA recorded a decision to forward his UFO inquiries to the Air Force's public information office to be answered there, and to treat that as a precedent for all such inquiries. No record opened here gives an end date for his directorship.
